section: A. Confidence Interval for Population Mean
q: A confidence interval for a population mean is primarily used to:
options: Estimate a population parameter using a range of values
Test whether two variables are independent
why: A confidence interval reports a plausible range for an unknown parameter, not a single exact value.

section: A. Confidence Interval for Population Mean
q: When the population standard deviation σ is known, a confidence interval for the population mean is generally constructed using:
why: With σ known (and a normal sampling distribution), the z-distribution supplies the critical value.

section: A. Confidence Interval for Population Mean
q: A sample has x̄ = 50, σ = 10, and n = 100. For 95% confidence, z = 1.96. What is the margin of error?

section: A. Confidence Interval for Population Mean
q: If the confidence level is increased from 95% to 99%, with everything else unchanged, the confidence interval will generally:
why: Higher confidence needs a larger critical value, so the interval stretches.

section: A. Confidence Interval for Population Mean
q: Increasing the sample size generally causes a confidence interval to:
why: Standard error is σ/√n, so a bigger n shrinks it and tightens the interval.

section: B. Confidence Interval for Population Proportion
q: Which statistic is used as the point estimate of population proportion p?
why: The sample proportion p̂ estimates the population proportion p.

section: B. Confidence Interval for Population Proportion
q: In a survey of 500 customers, 400 are satisfied. What is the sample proportion?

section: B. Confidence Interval for Population Proportion
q: The estimated standard error of a sample proportion is:
why: SE(p̂) = √[p̂(1-p̂)/n]. The other forms apply to means, not proportions.

section: B. Confidence Interval for Population Proportion
q: A 95% confidence interval for a population proportion is (0.72, 0.80). Which interpretation is appropriate?
options: Exactly 76% of all customers are satisfied
We are 95% confident that the population proportion lies between 0.72 and 0.80
The probability that every customer is satisfied is 0.95
why: Confidence refers to the long-run procedure capturing the population proportion, not to individual customers.

section: C. Hypothesis Testing for Population Mean
q: A company claims its average delivery time is 3 days. To test whether the actual mean differs from 3 days, the null hypothesis is:
why: The null always states the claimed value with equality: μ = 3.

section: C. Hypothesis Testing for Population Mean
q: For the previous question, the appropriate alternative hypothesis is:
why: "Differs from" has no direction, so the alternative is two-sided: μ ≠ 3.

section: C. Hypothesis Testing for Population Mean
q: If the p-value is 0.02 and α = 0.05, what should we conclude?
why: p = 0.02 < α = 0.05, so reject H₀. Note we never 'accept' H₀ as proven.

section: C. Hypothesis Testing for Population Mean
q: A Type I error occurs when we:
options: Fail to reject a false null hypothesis
Fail to reject a true null hypothesis
why: Type I error = rejecting a null that is actually true (a false positive), with probability α.

section: C. Hypothesis Testing for Population Mean
q: A Type II error occurs when we:
options: Fail to reject a false H₀
why: Type II error = failing to reject a null that is actually false (a false negative), with probability β.

q: To compare the mean delivery times of Warehouse A and Warehouse B, the usual null hypothesis for a two-sided test is:
why: A two-sided comparison of two means is written as a zero difference: μA - μB = 0.

q: Two samples are independent when:
options: The same subjects are measured twice
Observations in one group do not correspond to observations in the other group
why: Independence means the observations in one group are unrelated to those in the other.

q: A two-mean test gives p = 0.37 at α = 0.05. The correct decision is:
options: Conclude the means are exactly equal
why: p = 0.37 is far above α = 0.05, so there is not enough evidence to reject H₀.

q: A paired t-test is most appropriate for:
options: The same employees before and after training
why: Pairing applies when the same units are measured twice, such as before and after training.

q: A chi-square goodness-of-fit test determines whether:
options: An observed categorical distribution matches an expected distribution
why: Goodness-of-fit compares an observed frequency distribution with an expected one.

q: Which expression contributes to a chi-square statistic?
why: Each cell contributes (O-E)²/E, and these are summed over all categories.

q: A store expects 400 orders to be equally distributed among four categories. Expected frequency per category is:
why: Equal distribution gives 400/4 = 100 expected orders per category.

q: For a goodness-of-fit test with 5 categories and no estimated parameters, degrees of freedom are:
why: df = k - 1 = 5 - 1 = 4 when no parameters are estimated from the data.

q: A chi-square test of independence determines whether:
options: A population mean equals a specified value
Two numerical variables have equal means
why: The test of independence checks whether two categorical variables are associated.

q: To test whether Payment Method and Customer Age Group are associated, use:
why: Both variables are categorical, so the chi-square test of independence applies.

q: For a 3 × 4 contingency table, degrees of freedom are:
Expected frequency for a cell in a contingency table is:
why: Expected = (Row total × Column total)/Grand total.

q: One-way ANOVA is primarily used to compare:
options: Means of three or more groups
why: ANOVA compares the means of three or more groups in a single test.

q: For comparing mean delivery times among Standard, Express and Same-Day delivery, the ANOVA null hypothesis is:
why: The null asserts all group means are equal: μ₁ = μ₂ = μ₃.

q: ANOVA gives p = 0.003 at α = 0.05. We conclude:
options: At least one population mean differs
why: A small p-value rejects equality, telling you at least one mean differs — but not which one.

q: A large ANOVA F-statistic generally indicates:
options: Between-group variation is large relative to within-group variation
why: F is the ratio of between-group to within-group variation, so a large F means group differences dominate.

section: H. Basics of Matrices and Operations
q: If matrix A has 3 rows and 4 columns, its order is:
why: Order is stated rows × columns, so 3 × 4.

section: H. Basics of Matrices and Operations
q: Two matrices can be added if:
why: Addition is element-wise, so both matrices must have identical dimensions.

H. Basics of Matrices and Operations
q: If A is 3 × 4 and B is 4 × 2, the dimension of AB is:
why: Inner dimensions cancel and the outer ones remain: (3×4)(4×2) → 3 × 2.

section: H. Basics of Matrices and Operations
q: For A(m × n)B(p × q), AB exists when:
why: The inner dimensions must match, so n = p.

section: H. Basics of Matrices and Operations
q: Which statement about matrix multiplication is generally true?
why: Matrix multiplication is not commutative in general, so AB ≠ BA.

section: H. Basics of Matrices and Operations
q: The transpose of [[1,2,3],[4,5,6]] is:
why: Transposing turns rows into columns: [[1,4],[2,5],[3,6]].

section: H. Basics of Matrices and Operations
q: For an identity matrix I, which property is correct?
why: The identity is the multiplicative neutral element, so AI = IA = A.

If population σ is unknown and the sample is small, with an approximately normal population, which distribution is typically used for a mean confidence interval?
why: With σ unknown and a small sample from a roughly normal population, use Student's t.

q: A sample has n = 25. For a one-sample t confidence interval for the mean, the degrees of freedom are:
Which change decreases the margin of error, all else equal?
why: Margin of error is z·σ/√n, so raising n is the only listed change that shrinks it.

q: A 95% CI for mean delivery time is (2.8, 3.4) days. Is μ = 3.0 compatible with the interval?
why: 3.0 lies inside (2.8, 3.4), so it is a value the data are consistent with.

Which statement correctly describes a 95% confidence procedure?
options: 95% of observations must fall inside every interval
In repeated sampling, about 95% of intervals constructed this way capture the true parameter
The parameter changes from sample to sample
The sample mean has a 95% probability of being correct
why: Confidence is a property of the repeated procedure: about 95% of such intervals capture the true parameter.

q: If the sample variability increases while n and confidence level remain fixed, the confidence interval for μ generally:
why: More variability inflates the standard error, so the interval widens.

q: A manufacturer claims mean package weight is 500 g. Which hypotheses test whether packages are underfilled on average?
why: 'Underfilled' is directional and below the claim: H₀: μ = 500 against H₁: μ < 500.

q: If α = 0.01, this means the researcher is willing to tolerate approximately what maximum probability of a Type I error?
why: α is the Type I error rate, so α = 0.01 means about a 1% chance.

q: If p-value = 0.08 and α = 0.05, the decision is:
why: p = 0.08 > α = 0.05, so there is insufficient evidence to reject H₀.

q: A test statistic measures:
options: How far the sample evidence is from the null value in standardized terms
The exact probability H₀ is true
why: A test statistic expresses the distance between sample evidence and the null value in standard-error units.

q: For H₁: μ > μ₀, the hypothesis test is:
why: A 'greater than' alternative puts the rejection region in the upper tail.

q: For H₁: μ < μ₀, the hypothesis test is:
why: A 'less than' alternative puts the rejection region in the lower tail.

q: For H₁: μ ≠ μ₀, the test is:
why: A 'not equal' alternative splits the rejection region across both tails.

q: A sample of 100 deliveries has x̄ = 52 minutes. Under H₀, μ₀ = 50, σ = 10. The Z statistic is:
If a 95% two-sided confidence interval for μ₁-μ₂ does not contain 0, what is the corresponding conclusion at α = 0.05?
options: Fail to reject equality of means
The means must differ by exactly 1
why: An interval for μ₁-μ₂ excluding 0 matches rejecting equality at the same α.

q: Statistical significance necessarily means:
options: The observed evidence is sufficiently inconsistent with H₀ at the chosen α
why: Significance is a statement about evidence against H₀ at the chosen α — it says nothing about practical importance.
